subject: Oceanography
title: Nutrient Pollution
description: A fast breakdown of Nutrient Pollution for builders.

hook.text: Fertilizer washed from farms into the sea creates 'dead zones'—areas where nothing can breathe.

buildup.text: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus fuel algal blooms—massive growths that block light and consume oxygen.

discovery.text: When the algae die and decompose, bacteria consume all available oxygen—suffocating fish and shellfish.

twist.text: The Gulf of Mexico dead zone reaches 15,000 km² each summer—fed by the Mississippi River's farm runoff.

climax.text: Over 500 dead zones now exist worldwide—doubling every decade since the 1960s.

punchline.text: Feeding crops on land is starving the sea of oxygen.

quiz.question: What causes ocean dead zones?
options: Excess nutrients trigger algal blooms that consume oxygen
